source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Numbers 5–6. All 58 exact original records are hashed, with no note elements in this scope. Later book numbering differences require separate mapping.

key_decisions.decision: Preserves all three excluded groups; avoids equating tsaraat with a single modern diagnosis and retains corpse-related uncleanness.
Keeps both sexes, repeated expulsion, the plural camps and divine dwelling as the stated reason; does not recast exclusion as voluntary.
Preserves the explicit inclusion of men and women, the general human-sin wording and breach of faith with the LORD; notes the alternative against-others reading.
Clarifies the parties without adding death explicitly; retains the family redeemer, payment to the LORD for the priest and separate ram.
Takes the first ownership pronoun as referring to the donor and makes the second recipient explicit; a note preserves the alternative priest referent.
Keeps the sex-specific marriage relationship and conditional opening rather than treating every accused woman as already guilty.
Makes sexual intercourse explicit, retains secrecy, absence of witnesses and not-being-caught, without adding an established verdict.
Preserves the repeated jealousy language and both guilty and innocent possibilities before the procedure follows.
Keeps husband as actor, barley amount, both prohibited additives and the jealousy/remembrance/guilt relationship.
Keeps the repeated standing, action on her hair, distinct items in her hands and his, and bitter curse-bearing water; notes uncovering as an alternative.
Retains the oath, innocence condition and under-husband expression, with harm exemption rather than an assumption of guilt.
Preserves the contrasting condition and interrupted speech without inventing its completion before the priest’s curse formula.
Retains oath and curse, divine agency and bodily images without silently choosing miscarriage or infertility as a precise diagnosis.
Keeps the body effects in their reversed order, curse-bearing water and the woman’s doubled response.
Keeps coercive priestly agency, repeated curse/water language and bitterness; notes the later resumption of drinking in verses 26–27.
Retains the conditional guilt, actual threatened bodily harm and public curse without giving a medical mechanism or assuming pregnancy.
Preserves the innocent alternative and seed-related fertility outcome, with the literal expression explained in a note.
Retains the alternative suspicion case, husband’s presentation and priest’s full procedure; does not merge suspicion into established wrongdoing.
Preserves the asymmetrical closing statement and bear-guilt idiom; does not add a punishment for the husband or erase the innocent outcome in verse 28.
